review_candidates.title: Data Engineer
review_candidates.description: Role We're hiring a data engineer to own our metrics layer: the governed, single-source-of-truth definitions of every business metric, computed in SQL on the warehouse and served to Power BI and other downstream consumers. This is a backend metrics role, not a dashboarding role — you make sure that when anyone in the company says "revenue" or "active user," there's exactly one formula behind it, defined once and reused everywhere. What you'll do Design, build, and maintain the SQL metrics/semantic layer on the warehouse. Enforce one canonical formula per metric across the entire data universe — no duplicated or drifting definitions. Model conformed dimensions and fact tables that keep Power BI filtering and cross-filtering correct. Build metrics compositionally: additive base components in SQL, with derived metrics (ratios, rates, averages) assembled from them so they re-aggregate correctly under any grouping. Own governance: naming standards, ownership, code review, automated tests, lineage, documentation, and deprecation. Above all, clear path for a (new) developer to consume and add new metrics without duplicating efforts. Set and enforce the policy for what's computed in SQL vs. left to Power BI / DAX. Optimize for query performance and cost — materialization strategy, incremental builds, pre-aggregation, partitioning/clustering. Must have Strong, idiomatic SQL — window functions, complex joins, and a real grasp of aggregation grain and additivity (why ratios and averages can't be summed). Hands-on Redshift and Databricks. Direct experience feeding Power BI: how model, relationships, and grain drive what filters and slicers actually do, and where DAX fits. Dimensional modeling: star schemas, conformed dimensions, SCDs, surrogate keys. Deep working knowledge of semantic/metrics-layer design principles (dbt Semantic Layer/MetricFlow, Cube, LookML, or equivalent). The concepts are essential even though no such tool will be procured or used here — you'll implement the same guarantees directly in SQL, so you must know what they do and why. A governance mindset — how to organize the project for multiple teams to collaborate on such project without duplication of efforts and schemas. Language: fluent Russian, Belarusian, or Ukrainian (working proficiency in at least one), plus fluent English. How we think about SQL vs. Power BI If a number’s definition must be identical everywhere, it lives in SQL — one formula, one owner. If a number only means something relative to what the user is currently viewing (filter-context time intelligence, dynamic ranking, what-if parameters), it can live in DAX. We store additive numerator/denominator components in SQL and form non-additive metrics at query time, so they respect any grouping the user applies rather than breaking at a fixed grain.
